title: Describe Data Using the Mean
objective: I can determine the mean of a data set, use a target mean to find a missing value, and explain the mean as the fair share and the balance point of the data.
model: mean as fair share (total shared equally) and as the balance point of a dot plot; target mean × count gives the total needed

widgets.component: Warm-up: add four counts, share 48 among 6, 17 ÷ 4, greatest of four decimals
widgets.root: Prerequisite skills for the mean (total, equal share, a decimal quotient, decimal order). Keys 44, 8, 4.25, 4.3 verified.

widgets.component: Mean of four / five numbers, Miguel's $60 over 4 days, Sofia's first four games
widgets.root: Keys verified (7, $15, 7, 14.75); items follow the worked example's 'combine, then share'.

widgets.component: Forgot to divide; divided by 5 instead of 4
widgets.root: Both are the lesson's named slips; fixes 9 and 10 verified.

widgets.component: Total / count / mean table; Sofia needs 150 in 10 games, has 133, needs 17
widgets.root: Table 36 ÷ 4, 90 ÷ 5, 60 ÷ 6 verified; the three Sofia items walk target total, current total, missing game (target mean × count).

widgets.component: Place a marker at the mean of 10, 12, 14, 16, 18
widgets.root: The five values are evenly spaced, so the mean equals the middle value and the median; a student who eyeballs the centre is right without computing or reasoning about balance.
widgets.replacement: Use skewed data on the line, e.g. 3, 4, 5, 6, 17 on a 0–20 line (mean 7, median 5): the student places the marker, then the check also asks 'Where is the median?'; trap the median (5) and the midpoint of the range (10). Keep step 2 and tolerance 0.

widgets.component: Mean from data, dot plot or fair share; missing value for a target mean
widgets.root: Sampled 120 seeds per level: meanFind L1 list, L2 'put together and share equally', L3 dot plot; meanMissing L1-L3 all use target mean × count − current total. Dot-plot keys recomputed (294 ÷ 14 = 21).

widgets.component: Drag the dots until the mean reaches a target; the triangle shows the balance point
widgets.root: Conditions are checked on the final dots (mean = target, range kept at L2), so many valid layouts exist and the live readout ties movement to the mean. Fair share is shown only in words, never as a levelling move.

widgets.component: 'How many points has Sofia scored in games 1 through 9?'
widgets.root: The nine scores (12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15, 10, 18) appear only in Practice §3 item 3; §5 is a separate mastery check that states no data, so the item cannot be answered on its own.
widgets.replacement: Restate the list in the stem: 'Sofia scored 12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15, 10 and 18 points in games 1–9. How many points has she scored in all?' Keep the key 133.
